title: Config Compliance Monitoring

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.1.15 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.1.15 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:config:notification` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" configRuleList{}.complianceType="NON_COMPLIANT"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.15_config_compliance_monito_15"
| sort -_time
description: AWS Config rules continuously evaluate resource compliance against security best practices. Non-compliant resources are attack surface.
value: Detecting config compliance monitoring early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable AWS Config with rules (e.g., CIS Benchmark). Forward Config notifications to SNS/S3 and ingest in Splunk. Dashboard showing compliance score per rule. Alert on newly non-compliant critical resources.
visualization: Table (resource, rule, status), Pie chart (compliant %), Bar chart by rule.
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Change.All_Changes
  where like(All_Changes.status, "%NON%") OR match(All_Changes.status, "(?i)non_?compliant|fail|error")
  by All_Changes.object All_Changes.user span=1h
| sort -count
dataModelAcceleration: Change: map `aws:config:notification` into All_Changes (resource as object, compliance as status). Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.
knownFalsePositives: New resources that have not been evaluated yet; rules you intentionally suppress during rollout; one-time exceptions on the change record.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:config:notification`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable AWS Config with rules (e.g., CIS Benchmark). Forward Config notifications to SNS/S3 and ingest in Splunk. Dashboard showing compliance score per rule. Alert on newly non-compliant critical resources.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" configRuleList{}.complianceType="NON_COMPLIANT"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.15_config_compliance_monito_15"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:config:notification` in `index=aws` to detect config compliance monitoring. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_15_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (resource, rule, status), Pie chart (compliant %), Bar chart by rule..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of config compliance monitoring so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
